subject.title: [Feature]: Load macOS onboarding providers from Gateway catalog

question: Should macOS Connect your AI consume a new additive Gateway setup-provider catalog and activate API-key choices through provider-owned auth methods, or should the first-run app keep a curated fixed provider list?
rationale: The missing behavior is clear, but the solution changes native onboarding UX, Gateway protocol shape, provider auth ownership, and secret/default-model activation semantics.

options.title: Adopt the Gateway catalog path
options.body: Expose provider-owned text-inference API-key choices through an additive Crestodian setup payload and make the macOS picker consume it.

options.title: Keep a curated first-run list
options.body: Leave macOS onboarding limited to a small supported set and document CLI setup for long-tail providers.

options.title: Split protocol design first
options.body: Open or require a narrower protocol/API design before implementing the Swift picker and activation changes.

recommendation.title: Adopt the Gateway catalog path
recommendation.body: Expose provider-owned text-inference API-key choices through an additive Crestodian setup payload and make the macOS picker consume it.

likelyOwner.reason: This user owns the current macOS Connect your AI flow and opened the request for the next provider-catalog step.
